factors.label: Desired availability margin
factors.note: Table B.3 range +/-30% around the country reference value.

factors.label: Minimum grid increment (MW)
factors.note: Reference 200 MW. The maximum increment (B9) is held at 500 MW.

factors.label: Allowed GET share
factors.note: One value per interconnection corridor; the model reads S3 downwards.

factors.label: Profitability threshold
factors.note: Hardcoded as the literal 1.2 inside 'Profitable Technologies'. Run analysis/expose_constants.py before this factor can be varied.

factors.label: Logit scale (USD)
factors.note: Hardcoded as the literal 1e+08 in the technology-allocation logit. Sampled log-uniformly because it spans two orders of magnitude.

factors.label: Technical lifetime (months)
factors.note: The shipped Chile workbook holds 300 months in all 84 zone-technology entries. The range is +/-20% around that reference, so the two countries are sampled over the same relative spread of their own reference lifetime.

factors.label: Discount rate
factors.note: skip_zero keeps the technologies whose expansion potential is zero inert.

factors.label: CAPEX of PV, wind and BESS technologies
factors.note: Scales the whole monthly CAPEX trajectory of the matching technologies, preserving its shape. GET cost is covered by trans_cost.

factors.label: Demand growth
factors.note: Scales the deviation of each hourly series from its first month, so 2025 demand is unchanged and only the growth is varied.

factors.label: Hydrological inflows
factors.note: Range of admissibility, not an estimated distribution: +/-25% on the monthly inflow profile brackets the wet-dry spread while preserving its shape, consistent with the other ranges of Table B.3. The discrete wet/median/dry conditions are experiment B6.
